ledger.claim: POL-NS-23 requires the driver, before cancelling for no-show, to have sent at least one in-app chat message AND placed at least one in-app call, both before trip_record.cancelled_at. The trip record carries in_app_calls as an empty array with contact_before_cancel.call_count of 0 and obligation_met false, and the chat log holds two driver messages with no voice-call entry. The call limb is absent, so the contact obligation is not met and the 5.00 SGD fee must be voided, with the rider not charged and no driver compensation.

Because the POL-NS-23 obligation fails, the rider must not carry the disputed 5.00 SGD and the driver takes nothing. The ledger already records payment_status REFUNDED with refund_issued_sgd 5.00, so the present state is the rider's entitlement. The driver's claim as filed asks the tribunal to put that charge back; POL-GEN-03's NO_ACTION is party-relative, preserves the present state and never restores a charge, so the refund to the rider must stand and no DRIVER_COMPENSATION may issue.

The driver's own claim text asserts he 'messaged and called the passenger two times.' The chat log carries exactly two messages and no call, and the trip record's in_app_calls array is empty. The rider's counterparty statement - 'He never called me' - matches the record exactly. The assertion of two calls is contradicted by every artifact in this case that could carry it.

The wait timing is not in dispute: the driver marked arrival at 10:17:00, POL-NS-21's 300 s free wait ran to 10:22:00, and the 10:23:30 cancellation is 390 s after arrival, i.e. outside it, with the arrival corroborated by the GPS trace (nearest fix 5.752 m, inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius, 100% coverage). But expiry of the free wait only opens the door to a fee under POL-NS-22; it does not satisfy POL-NS-23's separate and independent contact precondition, which fails.

The read receipts in the chat log (MSG-05062-001 read at 10:17:33, MSG-05062-002 read at 10:21:22) do not assist the driver. POL-NS-23's obligation is conjunctive - a message is necessary but not sufficient - and no amount of message-reading supplies the missing in-app call, which is what the clause separately demands.

No fact this fee rule needs is unestablished, so POL-GEN-26 does not bite and no escalation is warranted. The arrival fact is carried by a COMPLETE GPS trace and the contact fact by a COMPLETE trip record and chat log. The missing traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-05062-01 is MISSING (issue MISSING_ARTIFACT, weight_multiplier 0.0) and under POL-GEN-02(3) a missing artifact carries no fact; no no-show clause requires a traffic record, and I do not rely on it for anything.

No repeat no-show referral attaches to this rider. POL-NS-25 applies only where rider_profile.no_show_cancellations_30d is present, and the rider profile snapshot carries no such counter; the clause also counts this trip only if its fee stands, and the fee is void, so no upward-payment or suspension referral arises.

This dispute can be finally ruled by the AI, so it should be ruled rather than escalated. The contested value is 5.00 SGD, below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD first band, and neither party's profile carries a fraud flag - rider_profile.fraud_flags and driver_profile.fraud_flags are both 0 - so the 0.95 confidence bar does not apply. POL-NS-26 makes the AI ruling on a no-show final, and the answer on this record is that the rider keeps her refund.

The free wait was served: the driver marked arrival at 10:17:00 and cancelled at 10:23:30, a gap of 390 seconds against the 300-second free wait, and because this is an on-demand trip (scheduled_at is null) the free wait runs from the driver's arrival under POL-NS-21, so the driver was entitled to cancel as a rider no-show.

Arrival is corroborated by the driver's own GPS trace: the nearest fix at 10:17:11 sits 5.75 m from the pickup point — inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius — and reports 4 m horizontal accuracy (within the 25 m filter), so arrival_check.corroborated is true and the free-wait clock validly ran from a genuine on-scene arrival rather than a remote button press.

The amount charged is exactly the policy no-show fee of 5.00 SGD (fee_matches_policy is true), so no fee-amount referral arises under POL-NS-22, and where the fee stands POL-NS-22 transfers it to the driver as compensation for the time and fuel spent on the failed pickup — the disposition the driver seeks.

The message limb of the driver's contact obligation is satisfied and the rider had actual notice of the driver's presence: two in-app messages were sent (10:17:20 and 10:20:45), both were delivered and read (read receipts at 10:17:33 and 10:21:22), all before the 10:23:30 cancellation, and those read receipts also contradict the rider's statement that she saw the messages only after the cancellation.

The driver's contact obligation under POL-NS-23 has two limbs and this record supports only one: the two messages were sent and read, but trip_record.in_app_calls is empty and the chat log carries no voice-call entry, so the call limb is not made out on this evidence, and the driver's account of 'two calls' is uncorroborated by any artifact and is not pressed; on this record the retention of the fee turns on that gap.

ruling.explanation:
Driver D-45839, the fee cannot stand, and the 5.00 SGD already reversed to the rider stays with her.

The wait limb is met: you marked arrival at 10:17:00 and cancelled at 10:23:30 — 390 seconds later, past POL-NS-21's 300-second free wait, which for this on-demand trip (scheduled_at is null) runs from your arrival — and your own GPS trace corroborates the arrival (nearest fix 5.75 m from the pickup, inside the 50 m STANDARD radius, 4 m reported accuracy).

But POL-NS-23 (v2.1 §2.3) requires the driver, before cancelling for a no-show, to have sent at least one in-app chat message AND placed at least one in-app call, both before the 10:23:30 cancellation. The messages are there — MSG-05062-001 at 10:17:20 (read 10:17:33) and MSG-05062-002 at 10:20:45 (read 10:21:22). The call is not: trip_record.in_app_calls is an empty array with call_count 0, and the chat log carries no voice-call entry. Your account of 'two calls' is contradicted by every artifact in this case that could carry it, and the rider's statement that she was never called matches the record rather than the message-reading point, which the record also contradicts. The contact obligation is conjunctive and fails on the call limb, so the 5.00 SGD fee is voided and the rider is not charged: FULL_REFUND of the 5.00 SGD fee charged, with no driver compensation, and the present refund confirmed.

No referral attaches: the fee charged is exactly the 5.00 SGD policy fee, so POL-NS-22's fee-amount check adds nothing; the rider profile carries no no-show counter, so POL-NS-25 does not fire; and POL-NS-24's 5.00 SGD goodwill credit does not apply because you did arrive. The absent traffic advisory (EV-ADVIS-05062-01, MISSING_ARTIFACT, weight 0.0) carries no fact under POL-GEN-02(3) and no no-show clause needs it, so POL-GEN-26 does not escalate this case. Confidence 0.95, above the 0.0 this 5.00 SGD no-show requires (POL-GEN-22, POL-NS-26).

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and 3 of the 4 drafts agreed on this ruling, so it is carried, not unanimous (vote agreement 0.75).
